Concept Revision 2 — Focused Refinement Pass

Same direction. Sharper edges.

This is not a new territory and not a rebuild. Territory A still governs structure, Territory B still carries Russ's voice and warmth, Territory C still stays confined to genuine archive. This pass adds a real dark theme, rebuilds the header, tests an alternate action system, and gives Expertise the depth the other pages already had.

How to read this document

Every mockup frame carries a light/dark theme toggle-pill so you can see both states of the same content. Anything genuinely experimental — not a fix, a real fork in the road — carries an Owner review tag and is shown next to the current version, never silently swapped in.

Real content throughout: Russ's actual bio, admissions, clients, and citations, plus the real logo mark. No new photography exists — the photography section (13) works from what's actually available.

04

Theme-Toggle Prototype

A real, working toggle — click it. This is the interaction the production header control should perform, demonstrated live rather than just described.

Interactive — click "Light" / "Dark" below Home opening, condensed
ryanlegalpc.com
Ryan Legal, PC
ExpertiseAboutContact
PaymentSchedule a Consultation

Ryan Legal, PC — Fresno, California

Thirty-five years of experience. Direct access to the attorney handling your matter.

AV PreeminentSuper Lawyer since 201490%+ record

Production behavior this demonstrates: on first visit, detect prefers-color-scheme and render that theme immediately — a small inline script in <head>, before CSS paints, so there's no flash of the wrong theme. Once a visitor taps the toggle, that choice is explicit and persists (e.g. localStorage), overriding the system preference until they change it again. The control itself needs a real accessible name (aria-label="Theme", or a visible "Light / Dark" label as shown here — never an icon alone). Contrast gets checked independently in both states, not assumed from one pass.

The monogram treatment in the About section (Section 9) works with zero new photography. An eye-level, naturally lit iPhone portrait can replace it later, only if she's comfortable being photographed — never required.

Retire from the repo

public/attorney-writing.webp — a generic stock photo of an anonymous suit signing papers next to a gavel and scales of justice — is exactly the imagery this whole direction has been arguing against. It should not carry over into the rebuild regardless of which Expertise option ships.

iPhone capture guide — no professional shoot required:

  • Shoot in natural daylight — morning or late afternoon, not overhead fluorescent
  • Avoid the ultra-wide lens; it bends door frames and desk edges
  • Keep vertical lines (door frames, window edges) actually vertical
  • Clear temporary clutter — stray cables, paper stacks, coffee cups — before shooting
  • Take both landscape and portrait versions of anything promising
  • Leave empty space around the subject so a responsive crop has room to work with
  • Take several exposures and angles of each subject — pick the best afterward, don't commit to the first shot
14

Final Recommendation

Answering the questions this revision was actually asked to answer.

Yes

Did the revision improve the design without losing Revision 1's strengths?

Home, About, Contact, and Payment are structurally untouched. What changed is additive: dark mode, the header, Expertise, and a handful of clearly-flagged experiments.

Yes

Does the dark theme feel native rather than added afterward?

It's built from its own ground color, not an inverted paper background — and the header/footer staying navy in both themes is the detail that sells it as one system.

Yes

Is the redesigned header more distinctive and more functional?

The typeset wordmark plus the logo's own hairline rule reads as considered rather than a stock template header — and it finally fixes the cramped two-line logo problem.

Partly

Are blue and gold being used with more sophistication?

The editorial proof treatment and the experimental button system both dial gold back to a detail rather than a fill. The gold-solid CTA still earns its place for the single most important action on a page — that's a deliberate exception, not an oversight.

Yes

Is Expertise now as resolved as the other major pages?

It has an opening composition, a persistent index, a real practice-section pattern, and breakpoint behavior for the first time — it was the weakest page and is no longer the weakest page.

Mostly

Did reducing pills improve editorial authority or remove useful clarity?

The editorial proof treatment reads more confident in a hero or a credential strip. Pills still win for dense, scannable metadata — Expertise's client-type tags, for instance — so this was a hierarchy fix, not a pill ban.

Undecided

Do the revised links and buttons actually outperform the originals?

For Payment and text links, yes, clearly. For the primary consultation CTA, the original solid gold button is arguably still stronger on mobile — this is exactly why it's flagged, not adopted outright.

Yes

Does the site still feel personable and respectable rather than casual?

Nothing in this revision pushes further toward casual — if anything, the editorial proof treatment and the lighter About rail both read slightly more composed than Revision 1.

Which experimental changes should move forward?

Accept outright: dark theme, the header rebuild, and the Expertise rebuild — none of these were close calls. Accept with the owner's sign-off: the quiet Payment/text-link treatment from the button experiment, the About mobile jump menu, and the simplified Contact panel hierarchy. Keep open, pending Russ's own read: the headline, the quotation treatment, and the Contact headline — none of the alternatives shown here are assumed to have already won.
